subject: Bridger AI — integration recap: embeddings+ranks, function-calls & streaming
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@bridger.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridger.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T14:12:00+00:00
Subject: Bridger AI — integration recap: embeddings+ranks, function-calls & streaming

Hi Sarah + Liam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment. TL;DR: Bridger's main goals are (1) 20–50ms embedding vector generation at scale, (2) deterministic reranking for search results, and (3) progressive streaming for UX with structured function outputs for downstream processing.

Key pain points you shared:
- Embedding latency spikes during batch imports (current pipeline stalls at peaks).
- Reranker consistency: model outputs vary by prompt context and you want predictable ordering for compliance audits.
- UI experience: you want immediate partial results (streaming) while the full structured output (function call) finishes.

What we discussed (product fit):
- SDK & integration: Redwood's SDK has a thin patch we can propose to avoid rewriting your existing client code. The patch wires streaming hooks and exposes function-calling primitives that return structured JSON payloads you can validate on-receive.
- Embeddings pipeline: prefix caching + warmup batching will reduce 95th percentile token latency during imports; for smaller vectors we recommend the 8-bit quantization profile we discussed to cut memory without large quality loss.
- Reranking: two approaches — (A) offload initial candidate generation to your current retriever, then call Redwood reranker with explicit context and tie-break signals, or (B) run reranker as a post-filter with deterministic temperature=0 prompt templates. We sketched both; we should run a small A/B eval.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) REDWOOD (Jonas/Dev): share a short integration checklist + the SDK patch and a proposed canary rollout plan. Attachment: "redwood-sdk-proposed-patch.diff".
2) BRIDGER (Sarah): share a sample of your embedding import job (anonymized) and target throughput (qps/avg vector size).
3) TECH CALL: propose a 60-min tech deep-dive next week to walk Dev and Neha through your pipeline and validate the patch.
4) COMPLIANCE: Bridger to flag any security concerns; Laura will attach SOC2 evidence and architecture notes.

Proposed slots for the deep-dive (UTC): Tue 2026-03-03 10:00, Wed 2026-03-04 14:00, Thu 2026-03-05 09:00. Tell me what works and I'll send the invite.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-sdk-proposed-patch.diff (text/diff, 12KB)]

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@bridger.ai>

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridger.ai>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@bridger.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T08:07:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Bridger AI — integration recap: embeddings+ranks, function-calls & streaming

Thanks Jonas — solid recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before the tech call:

1) Sample data: we can provide a gzipped CSV of 25k anonymized records (text length distribution included). We'll share by EOD Monday.
2) Throughput targets: steady-state ingestion 200 qps, occasional spikes to 800 qps for backfills. Our current retriever returns ~150 candidates per query.

Technical Qs (so Dev/Neha can prep):
- Will the SDK patch be compatible with our existing Node.js ingestion service (v16)? We prefer minimal footprint changes.
- For streaming partials: can we get an event schema (examples) so our frontend engineers can wire the progress indicators?
- Reranking latency SLO: can you target <100ms p95 for a 150-candidate rerank on a single c5.4xlarge equivalent? If not, what are the tradeoffs?

We also have one security ask: we need to know if Redwood's batch imports can be configured to avoid retention of raw text on your side (metadata-only caching).

We'll take Tue 2026-03-03 10:00 (works best). Please send the invite.

—Sarah
Sarah Jennings
Head of Search, Bridger AI
[sarah.jennings@bridger.ai]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@bridger.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridger.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:23:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Bridger AI — integration recap: embeddings+ranks, function-calls & streaming

Perfect — thanks for the details, Sarah. A few quick notes ahead of Tuesday's deep-dive: 

Compatibility: the SDK patch is Node-compatible and we've validated it on v14–v18; Dev will bring a short demo to show how little code changes are required.

Streaming schema: attaching a short example in the integration checklist ("bridger-integration-checklist.xlsx") — the streaming event types are: PARTIAL_TEXT, KVCACHE_WARMUP, FUNCTION_CALL_START, FUNCTION_CALL_COMPLETE (structured JSON payload). We'll paste sample payloads into the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-bridger-eval

Reranker latency: for 150 candidates we expect p95 ~60–120ms depending on model size and quantization. Two quick levers to guarantee <100ms p95: reduce candidate set returned by retriever (we can add a cheap filter), or use a smaller reranker variant with tuned prompt/score calibration. Dev will bring benchmark numbers and a canary plan.

Data retention: yes — batch imports can be configured to avoid persistent raw-text retention. We support ephemeral-only ingest for pipeline jobs and will provide the exact config + SOC2 section that describes auditability. Laura will attach the relevant doc during the call.

I've scheduled the 60-minute technical deep-dive for Tue 2026-03-03 10:00 UTC and sent a calendar invite. Agenda: 1) sample data walkthrough (15m), 2) SDK patch demo and streaming example (20m), 3) reranker benchmarking and quantization options (15m), 4) rollout & next steps (10m).

Deliverables before the call:
- REDWOOD: full checklist + sample streaming payloads + SDK patch (attachments included).
- BRIDGER: anonymized sample dataset + throughput target confirmation.

If anything changes, flag it in this thread. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Thanks — Jonas
